_note: Single source of truth for the on-device / host microbenchmarks under test/performance_benching. Never hand-edited: use test/performance_benching/bench.py (bench add / bench update), then bench gen to rewrite each project's platformio.ini.

cellularum.desc:
On-device cycle-counter A/B for the bounded-run string entries (cellularum_laboro) against the target's own libc, across input lengths 8 to 2048: cellul.len vs strnlen, cellul.chr vs strchr, cellul.diff vs memcmp, and cellul.find vs strstr, plus dispatch_len8 against direct_len8 to price MMGR_CALL itself.
The libc side is ESP-ROM - strnlen, strchr, memcmp and strstr all resolve into the part's mask ROM as hand-written assembly, running without flash-cache pressure, while the library runs from flash through the icache. The comparison is against that, not against a portable C libc, and not against a desktop one: a desktop libc answers these with SSE or AVX and neither part has anything of the kind.
Lengths start at 8 because a fixed prologue cannot show at one size alone and the crossover is the reading. The buffer is aligned and fixed, since the library is built for memory that arrives aligned and an unaligned fixture would time a head walk it never performs.
Build and flash (both parts carry USB-Serial/JTAG):
idf.py -C test/performance_benching/cellularum -B build_esp32s3 -D SDKCONFIG=sdkconfig.esp32s3 set-target esp32s3
ninja -C test/performance_benching/cellularum/build_esp32s3 -j 2
idf.py -C test/performance_benching/cellularum -B build_esp32s3 -p COM4 flash
then open the port to capture the repeating "DB ..." lines (each run repeats every ~5 s, so a capture opened at any time still catches a full cycle). Substitute esp32c6 and its port for the RISC-V part.
Cap the job count: ninja defaults to cores + 2, and a full IDF tree at that width took the build machine down.

memoria.desc:
On-device cycle-counter A/B for the region entries (memoria_operor) against the target's own libc, across input lengths 8 to 2048: memor.cmp vs memcmp, memor.chr vs memchr, memor.cpy vs memcpy, and memor.set vs memset.
The libc side is ESP-ROM hand-written assembly running without flash-cache pressure, while the library runs from flash through the icache. The comparison is against that, not against a portable C libc.
cmp and chr walk a word at a time; cpy and set move four words an iteration, which is what it takes to hold ROM memcpy's rate rather than spend as much on the loop as on the move.
Build and flash (both parts carry USB-Serial/JTAG):
idf.py -C test/performance_benching/memoria -B build_esp32s3 -D SDKCONFIG=sdkconfig.esp32s3 set-target esp32s3
ninja -C test/performance_benching/memoria/build_esp32s3 -j 2
idf.py -C test/performance_benching/memoria -B build_esp32s3 -p COM4 flash
then open the port to capture the repeating "DB ..." lines. Substitute esp32c6 and its port for the RISC-V part. Cap the job count: ninja defaults to cores + 2, and a full IDF tree at that width took the build machine down.

praet.desc:
On-device cycle-counter comparison of three ways to pick a move direction from two addresses, at lengths 8, 64 and 2048.
memoria_operor has two moves and the caller picks: move_up when the destination is above the source, move_down when it is below, and the table points move_down at mmgr_memor_cpy because copying forward is already safe that way. Nothing inspects the two addresses and chooses. A DMA submit cannot be told, since both endpoints arrive as addresses, so something has to decide and this weighs what the deciding costs.
Three forms, all reaching the same two entries the same way: known, which is handed the answer and is the floor rather than a competitor; branch, which compares the two addresses; and mask, which builds an index from the same compare and takes it through a two entry table so nothing is predicted.
Three cases, because a branch is only expensive when it is wrong: destination above source every call, below every call, and alternating every call. Each head-to-head row is run in both orders, because on the C6 the arm that runs second has measured about 1.1 cycles more whatever it is, and a split that follows the position instead of the code is visible only by swapping.
Correctness runs before any timing. All three forms are checked against a byte-walk reference written in the bench rather than taken from the library, over a one byte overlap, a word apart in both directions, a half-length straddle and no overlap, at every length. A form that moves the wrong bytes still produces a number, and the number reads as a result.
Build and flash (both parts carry USB-Serial/JTAG):
idf.py -C test/performance_benching/praet -B build_esp32s3 -D SDKCONFIG=sdkconfig.esp32s3 set-target esp32s3
ninja -C test/performance_benching/praet/build_esp32s3 -j 2
idf.py -C test/performance_benching/praet -B build_esp32s3 -p COM3 flash
then open the port to capture the repeating "DB ..." lines. Substitute esp32c6 and its port for the RISC-V part. Cap the job count: ninja defaults to cores + 2, and a full IDF tree at that width took the build machine down.

verba.desc: Host and on-device A/B for the text and number writers (verba_scribo), and the rounding arms scale_to_u64 is given for a fixed-point tie.
